title: Proposal to Require USB-C to be Adopted as Charging Standard for Portable Electronics
what_it_is: Proposal to Require USB-C to be Adopted as Charging Standard for Portable Electronics

sections.label: E-waste measures and monitoring
sections.summary: India intends a similar requirement, most countries have not, and Singapore monitors developments while using Extended Producer Responsibility for e-waste.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: The Indian government intends to implement a similar requirement.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: But most countries have not announced similar measures.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: We are monitoring developments in this space, including manufacturers' response to the EU requirements.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: In the meantime, we have implemented other ways to manage e-waste, such as the Extended Producer Responsibility framework.

sections.label: EU measure reported effects
sections.summary: Reports state the EU measure will cut e-waste by 11,000 tonnes yearly and save consumers 250 million euros yearly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Reports state that the measure, when it comes into effect in the EU, will cut down e-waste by 11,000 tonnes a year and save consumers 250 million euros a year.

sections.label: Monitoring developments
sections.summary: The short answer is that developments in this space are still being monitored.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: The short answer is that we are still monitoring developments in this space.
